subject: Day 30: one month; routines firming; help-network check
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 30. One month. Feeding cadence is steady, social smiles are appearing more reliably, and head control is visibly stronger. With the harder weeks ahead, this is the right day to firm up the help network rather than improvise it later.

Action items
- List the two or three people you can call at 2am for an extra set of hands — a relative, a postpartum doula, a close friend. Confirm each is actually willing and on the same coast.
- Settle a working evening-rotation plan between Anoushka and Noah for the cluster-fussy hours; write it on the fridge so it is not renegotiated at the moment of need.
- Verify Avi is covered on the health-insurance plan and the insurance card or member number is accessible from your phone. Healthcare.gov on qualifying life events: https://www.healthcare.gov/glossary/qualifying-life-event/
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is scheduled. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Evening cluster fussiness; hiccups during or after feeds; quiet startle to loud sounds.
- [low concern] Brief head lifts during tummy time; social smiles consolidating.
- [monitor] Caregiver burnout signals — short fuse, dread of evenings, persistent low mood — name them out loud before the worst night.
- [call within 24h] Sustained feeding refusal. Forceful projectile vomiting. Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Tummy time 20-30 minutes a day across multiple bouts. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Read aloud 15 minutes a day.
- Live singing during low-stress routines like diapering and bathing.
- Outdoor walk in the stroller for 20-30 minutes most days — vitamin D for him and cardiovascular recovery for you. AAP HealthyChildren on vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 35-42: peak crying.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete
